name: Singapore
tagline: A city that lights its gardens and gave hawker food UNESCO status
hero_description: Singapore compresses a remarkable amount of spectacle into one clean, easy city: 50-metre Supertrees that perform a free light show nightly, the world's tallest indoor waterfall inside a misty dome (and another one at the airport), Universal Studios on its own resort island, and hawker centres whose food culture is UNESCO-listed. Five to six hours direct from Bengaluru, and four to five days covers it all.
best_time_to_visit: Genuinely year-round — November to March is pleasant and festive, while February to April sees the least rain; being equatorial, a brief afternoon shower is always possible.

top_attractions.name: Gardens by the Bay
top_attractions.description: A 101-hectare garden where 25–50 m Supertrees erupt into the free Garden Rhapsody light show every night — and the Cloud Forest dome hides a 35 m indoor waterfall in perpetual mist.

top_attractions.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
top_attractions.description: The observation deck bridging the three towers, looking down on the bay — while the free Spectra light-and-water show plays at the promenade below every evening.

top_attractions.name: Sentosa & Universal Studios
top_attractions.description: Singapore's resort island, reached by cable car or monorail — Universal Studios Singapore and the vast S.E.A. Aquarium anchor a full family day.

top_attractions.name: Night Safari
top_attractions.description: The world's first nocturnal wildlife park, open since 1994 — tram loops and walking trails through habitats that wake up after dark.

top_attractions.name: Hawker centres
top_attractions.description: Singapore's hawker culture holds UNESCO intangible-heritage status — chicken rice, laksa and satay done superbly for a few dollars at Maxwell or Lau Pa Sat.

top_attractions.name: Jewel Changi
top_attractions.description: The Rain Vortex — at roughly 40 m the world's tallest indoor waterfall — pours through the roof of the airport's forest-mall, worth scheduling your departure day around.

activities: Evening at the Supertree Grove light show after the Cloud Forest and Flower Dome
SkyPark views and the Spectra show from the Marina Bay promenade
Night Safari tram ride and walking trails
Hawker-centre food crawl through UNESCO-listed food culture
Heritage walk through Little India and Chinatown
Bumboat cruise on the Singapore River past the Merlion
Rain Vortex stop at Jewel Changi on departure day
